The sheet computes bearings from coordinate differences: D7 is the Easting difference (dE) and E7 is the Northing difference (dN). The key says quadrant 1 (N+, E+) uses no change, quadrant 2 (N-, E+) uses 180-RD, and quadrant 3 (N-, E-) uses RD+180. That is the standard azimuth calculation, so a single formula can handle all quadrants.

Bearing (azimuth) = ATAN2(dE, dN) in degrees, normalized to 0–360. In Excel, ATAN2(x_num, y_num) takes x first. Using dN as x and dE as y gives the angle from north: ATAN2(E7,D7) returns the angle whose tangent is D7/E7, i.e. dE/dN, which is the azimuth from north.

The formula needs to keep the result in 0–360, so I use MOD.

{"formula": "=MOD(DEGREES(ATAN2(E7,D7)),360)"}
